\n    const double cxx = (c[idx3(xp, y, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(xn, y, z, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dx * dx);\n    const double cyy = (c[idx3(x, yp, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, yn, z, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dy * dy);\n    const double czz = (c[idx3(x, y, zp, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, y, zn, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dz * dz);\n    \n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// Compute chemical potential\nvoid computeChemicalPotential(const std::vector<double>& c, std::vector<double>& mu,\n {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                const double cv = c[idx];\n                \n                mu[idx] = 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * e_BB - 2.0 ny) + y * nx + x;\n                const double pseudo = ((((linear_id + 1) * 1299709) % vol) / static_cast<double>(vol));\n                c[idx] = -1.0 + 2.0 * pseudo;\n            }\n        }\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1NwXZ4vpjogmrC1eQ9P","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark now runs entirely on the GPU, with no CPU fallback. It builds as `cahn_hilliard` with the same CLI and output format. On this RTX 3090 it is roughly 38–40× faster than the original CPU code at 256³ and 384³. One caveat up front: the results are not bit-identical to the CPU version, so the printed hash will differ.\n\n**What changed (only the two existing files)**\n- `cahn-hilliard/cahn_hilliard.cpp`: the chemical potential, the Cahn-Hilliard update, and the initialization are CUDA kernels, using 3D thread blocks (32×4×4) with grid-stride loops. The field stays on the device for all steps, with no host sync per step, and is copied back once after the timed loop. Arithmetic order is unchanged. The host still does the `-r` printing and `-v` validation.\n- `cahn-hilliard/CMakeLists.txt`: enables the CUDA language, compiles the existing `.cpp` as CUDA (no new files), and requires CMake 3.24+ and CUDA Toolkit.\n\n**Decisions I made**\n- **Architectures:** `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` is set to `70 75 80 86 89 90`, overridable with `-D`. I first used `native`, but CMake resolved it to `sm_52` here, so I replaced it.\n- **Division skip:** the Laplacian divides by `dx*dx` three times per cell, and FP64 divide is very slow on this card. When the spacing is exactly 1.0, the divide is skipped (`x / 1.0 == x` exactly). Hashes are unchanged versus the non-skipping GPU build, and the general path still divides. This cut 256³ from 1033 ms to 395 ms per 200 steps.\n\n**Verification**\n- Built out-of-tree in `/tmp` with no warnings. Nothing was added to the project directory.\n- Compared against a CPU build of the original code over several shapes, including 1×1×1, non-cubic, and a 7×300000×1 grid. Hashes are not equal. Sample values differ by about 1e-17, and the sum differs by up to 4e-13 on 2M cells. This looks like floating-point rounding, but I did not pin it down. Turning off FMA contraction on nvcc didn't remove it.\n- `-v` passes on the GPU build at the sizes tested, and `-h` and unknown-option handling behave as before.\n\n**Timings (20 steps, ms)**\n\n| Grid | CPU (original) | GPU |\n|---|---|---|\n| 64³ | 31 | 1 |\n| 128³ | 256 | 6 |\n| 256³ | 2007 | 52 |\n| 384³ | 6818 | 168 |\n\n**Not verified:** the program has not been run on a machine without a GPU, where it would exit with a CUDA error by design. I did not test other GPU architectures or CUDA versions beyond 12.0."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":882,"cache_read_input_tokens":72977,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":882},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"94547771-4154-46d6-9e2c-b99716e5a8c0","uuid":"6ef7419b-2726-4aea-a4ba-5e75b666e12e","timestamp":"2026-10-14T02:57:43.130Z","request_id":"req_011Cg1NwXFxjXbBcayN119y1"}
